subject: Vectorization and non-centered parameterization with nested groups

messages.author: 771657a10e2af316
messages.subject: Vectorization and non-centered parameterization with nested groups
parts:
Hi Stan users,


I’m trying to fit a hierarchical binomial-logit model with nested groups and am having some problems with vectorizing and implementing the the non-centered parameterization.


I’m working my way up to a more complex model, but to illustrate my problem I'll use an example of the effect of county-level healthcare funding on case-fatality rates. There is nesting as observations are reported from counties, which are nested within states. Each observation (row) indicates the number of deaths and a total number of cases, with multiple observations per county. In this case there is a small number of states (5).


First off, I was trying to use a vectorized non-centered parameterization, with the state and county effects in vectorized form in the transformed parameters block. However, I get divergent transitions which cannot be alleviated by increasing adapt delta. This plagued me for quite a while until I found a note from Bob saying that intermediate levels cannot (yet) be vectorized in Stan (http://stackoverflow.com/questions/29379001/nested-model-in-stan).


So then I tried a looped and centered version following his example, which included moving the state and county effects into the model block. 


This works (great!) but now that I’m attempting to implement the non-centered parameterization, I again get divergent transitions and I’m not sure why.


Any help to figure out the problem, or pointers on correct syntax for non-centered parameterizations with multiply nested groups would be greatly appreciated!


Attached is code to simulate data, as well as the three models. This is my first Stan model so I apologize if I’m making any obvious mistakes.



Max


P.S. I'm running Rstan 2.14.1

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Vectorization and non-centered parameterization with nested groups
parts:
You want to use the non-centered parameterizations when you
don't have much data and the centered parameterizations when
you do. You want to get rid of the funnel and tiled ellipses
in the posterior in favor of things that look a unit
circle (that happens when the parameters aren't correlated
in the posterior and have unit scales).

For vectorization, you can replace this:

vector[S] state_effect;
vector[C] county_mu;
vector[C] county_effect;

state_effect = sigma_state * state_raw;

for (c in 1:C)
county_mu[c] = beta_funding * funding[c] + state_effect[state[c]];

county_effect = county_mu + sigma_county * county_raw;

with

vector[C] county_effect = beta_funding * funding
+ sigma_state * state_raw[state]
+ sigma_count * count_raw;

And then you can just drop it into the regression along with beta0
unless you want to save it in the output. I find expanding things
all the way out like this is helpful because you can see the predictors
and the scales all in one place.

- Bob
